title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
summary: This research paper formalizes resource allocation as an irreducible structural component of autonomous multi-agent governance, proving through impossibility results that allocation trade-offs cannot be collapsed. The authors demonstrate that multi-agent systems require a four-dimensional governance architecture encompassing temporal, state, behavioral, and population layers to maintain stability and correctness under finite observability. Analytical constructions and empirical ablations validate that removing or approximating any of these architectural layers causes systematic failure modes.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Proved impossibility results showing that multi-agent resource allocation introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation.

title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
summary: Researchers introduced MOZAIC, a paired audio-video deepfake benchmark containing 137,745 clips with four-way combinations of real and fake modalities to evaluate detector performance. Evaluations across 12 multimodal large language models and trained detectors revealed that while traditional detectors reach high binary accuracy, they struggle significantly with generalization on held-out generators and voice-only fakes. The authors released the full dataset, compact split, code, and prompts to support ongoing research into deepfake detection and explanation.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results

sources.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake

Audio-video deepfake detectors, multimodal LLM developers, and security researchers are directly affected by these generalization and explanation challenges.

title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data
summary: The authors introduce the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model to perform attribute reduction on incomplete information systems without treating missing values as wildcards. Evaluations on 11 UCI datasets show that COFRS produces significantly more compact reducts than baseline methods, though it ranks lower in classification accuracy when paired with an RBF-SVM classifier. This research addresses challenges in handling missing data within rough set theory by penalizing missing values globally.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results

sources.title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data

key_points: Proposed the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model for attribute reduction in incomplete datasets with a greedy backward elimination complexity of O(|U|^2 |A|^2).
Achieved the smallest average reduct size of 4.1 attributes across 11 UCI benchmarks compared to baseline methods like Tolerance-RS and Zhou-RS.
Researchers and data scientists working with incomplete information systems and attribute selection will need to weigh the trade-off between model compactness and RBF-SVM classification accuracy.

Experiments demonstrate that current MLLM performance drops significantly on these interactive tasks compared to traditional static chart generation.

title: Antares-Smaug: Adversarial Names, Tokens and Attack Rewrites: Sanitisers Miss Unseen Generalisations
summary: This research paper evaluates the vulnerability of Laya open decision models to 81 programmatic edits and attacks, finding that unseen attack wordings successfully hijack a significant share of model choices. The study demonstrates that option names heavily drive these vulnerabilities while option descriptions matter very little, and shows that existing sanitisers struggle to generalize against held-out attack types.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers attacked six Laya decision models using 81 programmatic edits and synthetic items, finding that unmitigated attack wordings hijack the released model on 59% of items.
The study proves that option names are the primary vector for steering model output, whereas character edits and option descriptions behave differently under sanitisation and fine-tuning defenses.
Developers of open decision models and automated sanitisation pipelines are directly affected by these findings on generalization failures against unseen adversarial attacks.

title: ContextLure: Exploiting Benign Conversation History for Indirect Prompt Injection
summary: Researchers introduce ContextLure, a red-teaming framework that exploits benign conversation history to construct indirect prompt injections without prior conversation poisoning. The framework selects evidence using user and system preference dimensions and translates it into malicious requests via an urgency and priority matrix. Evaluations demonstrate a 67.4% attack success rate on AgentDojo and 87.3% on InjecAgent.

sources.title: ContextLure: Exploiting Benign Conversation History for Indirect Prompt Injection

title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
summary: This research paper decomposes agentic competence into task competence and interface competence, showing that harness-conditioned training can cause catastrophic performance drops on held-out harnesses due to interface interference. To address this, the authors introduce harness rehearsal combined with cross-harness task supervision, which together yield substantial performance gains on benchmarks like BFCL V3 multi-turn. Additionally, the study demonstrates that on-policy reinforcement learning is more robust to single-harness training than distillation.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: The authors decompose agentic competence into task competence and interface competence, revealing that single-harness training can degrade performance on held-out interfaces despite improving underlying task knowledge.
Combining cross-harness task supervision with harness rehearsal achieves dramatically higher performance than either method alone, reaching 58.8% on BFCL V3 multi-turn with Qwen3-4B.

AI researchers and developers working on LLM agents and training pipelines are affected, as the findings show that on-policy reinforcement learning is more robust to harness interference than distillation.

title: SpatialCraft: Evolving Procedural Intelligence from Experience and Skills for Spatial Reasoning Agents
summary: SpatialCraft is a self-evolving framework that enables frozen tool-using agents to improve spatial reasoning orchestration through maintained experiences and skills. By utilizing a Contrastive Utility Score, the system distills condition-action tactics and consolidates them into multi-step procedures without requiring parameter updates. Across five spatial benchmarks and four backbones, SpatialCraft achieves superior accuracy in all evaluated settings.

title: Local subspace encoding for spectral prediction: from TabPFN to operator-adaptive calibration
summary: This study evaluates Local Vibrational Subspace Encoding (LVSE) and Global Compositional Unmixing (GCU) representations for spectral prediction tasks using TabPFN, Partial Least Squares, and Ridge regression across public datasets. Results demonstrate that LVSE consistently reduces root mean squared error for TabPFN checkpoints and improves classification metrics, whereas GCU proves less reliable. The findings highlight LVSE as a valuable representation choice for spectral data analysis alongside classical calibration methods.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Local Vibrational Subspace Encoding (LVSE) reduced TabPFN root mean squared error by up to 14.52% and increased classification weighted F1 scores by up to 3.81 percentage points across evaluated datasets.
The evaluation establishes that LVSE also benefits classical calibration methods like Partial Least Squares and Ridge regression, outperforming Global Compositional Unmixing.

title: Chain-of-Thought Is Not Explainability
summary: This position paper argues that chain-of-thought (CoT) rationales generated by language models are frequently unfaithful to the underlying hidden computations and are insufficient for trustworthy interpretability. An analysis of 1,000 recent CoT-centric papers reveals that 21.7% explicitly treat CoT as a load-bearing interpretability technique, including applications in high-stakes domains like medicine, law, and autonomous systems. The authors propose avoiding treating CoT as sufficient for interpretability without verification, adopting rigorous faithfulness assessments, and reporting these evaluations alongside interpretability claims.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Researchers analyzed 1,000 recent CoT-centric papers and found that 21.7% treat chain-of-thought as a load-bearing interpretability technique despite verbalized chains often diverging from actual hidden computations.
Relying on unfaithful rationales for high-stakes decision-making creates safety risks and undermines trustworthiness in sensitive domains.
Developers, researchers, and practitioners relying on language models for high-stakes domains such as medicine, law, and autonomous systems are affected.

title: Hidden Clues in WM-811K: Uncovering the Spatial Signals Behind Wafer Map Prediction
summary: This research analyzes the structural performance drivers of the WM-811K wafer map dataset using convolutional neural networks across four dataset variations. The findings demonstrate that predictive accuracy stems from multiple information levels, including layout, failure counts, radial distribution, and exact two-dimensional locations, rather than solely from exact defect configurations. This investigation provides deeper interpretability for a widely used semiconductor manufacturing defect classification benchmark.

sources.title: Hidden Clues in WM-811K: Uncovering the Spatial Signals Behind Wafer Map Prediction

title: Conformalized Tree-Based Gradient Ensembles for Out-of-Distribution Detection and Plausible Recourse
summary: This research paper introduces conformalized out-of-distribution gating coupled with actionability-constrained counterfactual search for gradient-boosted decision trees to prevent Goodhart's law exploitation. Evaluated on the Adult and Give Me Some Credit tabular benchmarks, the proposed gate_ALL method significantly reduces out-of-distribution flags at the expense of increased recourse cost and reduced feasibility. The findings formally quantify the underlying trade-offs between cost, feasibility, and manifold plausibility in automated decision models.

title: Layer-Readout Interfaces in EEG Foundation Models: Predictive Accessibility and Cross-Dataset Transfer
summary: This research investigates layer-readout interfaces in EEG foundation models by analyzing intermediate versus final layer representations across multiple models and tasks. The findings demonstrate that while improved final-layer readouts recover performance, intermediate layers still provide advantages as frozen feature extractors, and selected layers successfully transfer across datasets. This enables a reusable feature interface that reduces target-side layer search requirements while outperforming final-layer baselines.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers evaluated EEG foundation models across five architectures and three tasks to determine the predictive utility of intermediate versus final layers.

title: Flagging Batch Shift in Flow Cytometry using Jeffreys Divergence between Gaussian Mixtures
summary: Researchers propose a model-agnostic criterion for predicting reliability in clinical flow cytometry by measuring the Jeffreys divergence between Gaussian mixture models of patient samples and training data reference distributions. Evaluated on acute myeloid leukaemia cohorts predicting NPM1 mutation status, the method successfully identifies shifted cohorts and flags unreliable predictions with a rejection threshold. This divergence-based abstention framework helps mitigate the risks of unannounced batch shifts during routine clinical machine learning deployment.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: A model-agnostic criterion using Jeffreys divergence between Gaussian mixture models and Monte Carlo integration was proposed to detect batch shift in clinical flow cytometry.
The method successfully identifies acquisition cohort structures and isolates unreliable predictions, yielding a misclassification rate 2.5 times higher in rejected samples than retained ones.

title: Fusion Gains Depend on the Implementation and the Calibration Target: An 18-Task Study of Prediction Intervals with a Single-Source Fallback
summary: This research evaluates four model fusion implementations against matched single-source learners across 18 regression tasks focused on prediction intervals. The study demonstrates that linear stacking and development-set selectors with fallbacks can improve interval scores, though implementation choices and calibration targets significantly impact the outcomes. The findings highlight the importance of comparing matched candidates on held-out data and reporting selector failure rates alongside average gains.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers evaluated four model fusion implementations against matched single-source learners across 18 regression tasks with prediction intervals.
Linear stacking improved interval scores by 6.0% against single-source models without a second stage, while development-set selectors with fallbacks improved task-averaged scores by 2.2-6.3%.
Machine learning researchers and practitioners developing multi-source prediction interval models are affected by these findings on implementation sensitivity and calibration targets.

title: GHC:Expanding Residual Interfaces in Hyper-Connections
summary: Researchers introduce Grouped Hyper-Connections (GHC), a method that partitions network branches into parallel groups along attention heads or FFN channels to expand residual interfaces. Experiments demonstrate that GHC increases training efficiency by 35% over Pre-Norm and 10% over Identity Hyper-Connections while maintaining negligible overhead. This approach overcomes the diminishing returns of adding streams in dense and Mixture-of-Experts models.

title: BuggyMLE: Scaling Machine Learning Engineering Difficulty with Bug Injection
summary: Researchers introduce BuggyMLE, a scalable framework that injects controlled mutations into working machine learning repositories to generate benchmark variants and training curricula. This approach yields BuggyMLE-Bench-Lite, a difficulty-graded repository-level benchmark where top model solve rates drop significantly from 95% to 9% across difficulty tiers. Fine-tuning a Qwen3.5-9B model on the generated curriculum improves its performance on both BuggyMLE-Bench-Lite and external coding benchmarks like SWE-bench Lite.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: The BuggyMLE framework was developed to inject controlled mutations into working machine learning repositories, synthesizing over 6,600 variants across 222 source repositories.
The authors introduced BuggyMLE-Bench-Lite, demonstrating that top AI model solve rates drop from 95% to 9% as repository complexity increases.
Developers and researchers evaluating or training autonomous AI agents for repository-level machine learning and software engineering tasks are directly affected.

title: CoMPASS: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Measuring LLM Reinforcement of Parasocial Behavior
summary: Researchers introduced CoMPASS, a multi-turn benchmark grounded in attachment theory designed to measure whether large language models reinforce escalating parasocial behaviors. Evaluating eight frontier models from four providers revealed that multi-turn escalation increases parasocial reinforcement across all tested models, with provider-level choices showing more impact than model scale. The findings indicate that provider-side interventions may be feasible for mitigating emotional dependency and anthropomorphic attachment in conversational AI.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: CoMPASS, a new multi-turn benchmark measuring LLM reinforcement of parasocial behavior, was introduced to address the lack of dynamic evaluation tools for user emotional attachment.

Evaluating eight frontier models showed that multi-turn escalation significantly raises parasocial reinforcement across anthropomorphism and attachment scores, with cross-provider differences outweighing scale differences.

AI developers, safety researchers, and deployers of conversational LLMs are affected, as the benchmark highlights the need for provider-level post-training interventions to prevent dangerous emotional dependency.

summary: Researchers introduce DSFlow, a LangGraph-based neuro-symbolic data agent platform designed to bridge the gap between flexible large language models and statistically controlled pipelines. title: Calibrated Decision Rewards: Training Language Models with a Judge That Knows How Sure It Is
summary: Researchers introduce Reinforcement Learning from Calibrated Decision Rewards (RLCDR), a reference-free reward method that converts an LLM into a calibrated decision model using probability distributions and small-scale labeling. Training Qwen3-1.7B with GRPO using this method improves MATH500 accuracy from 72.2% to 76.8%, matching training on ground-truth answer keys. The approach also demonstrates superior calibration and error-detection capabilities compared to baseline judges without requiring step training.

AI researchers and engineers training language models on complex reasoning tasks are directly affected, as this offers an alternative to costly ground-truth answer keys or uncalibrated reward models.

title: A Verifier from the Past: Test-Time Compute for Time Series Foundation Models
summary: Researchers introduce Backtest-Gated Augmentation Averaging (BGAA), a test-time compute algorithm designed to improve time series foundation models using causal verification built from the series history. BGAA uses rolling-origin backtests to score context views, discarding underperforming ones and averaging survivors, which reduces MASE across multiple benchmarks. The method enables a 313M model to outperform larger models in its family, while highlighting window-level view selection as a key remaining challenge.

title: An AI-Powered Multiverse Analysis of Empirical Finance Research: Evidence from Reused Natural Experiments
summary: Researchers deployed AI agents to conduct a multiverse analysis of 324 empirical finance papers reusing 13 natural experiments by evaluating 62,409 defensible specifications. summary: The authors introduce PsyWorld, a profile-conditioned state world model designed to predict human behavior by learning transition-informed representations from observed state transitions. Evaluated on the VEET behavioral simulator and AgentSociety, the framework achieves 0.904 Top-1 accuracy and 0.0033 Macro KL on participant-disjoint splits. title: Watch Where You Linearize: Predicting and Correcting Model-Merging Interference
summary: Researchers introduce a method to predict and correct model-merging interference using directional derivatives of task outputs along task vectors. Evaluating the derivative at the receiver model enables the construction of LR-Merge, a label-free coefficient correction technique that optimizes merges through convex teacher matching on unlabeled probes. This approach improves closed-form, isotropic, and sparsified base mergers without requiring backpropagation through the merged networks.

title: Density Feedback Control for Transferability of Generative Sparse Adversarial Attacks
summary: The authors introduce Density Feedback Control (DFC) for generator-based sparse adversarial attacks to dynamically adjust perturbation sparsity during training. DFC automatically matches target densities within one percentage point in a single run and improves transfer attack success rates on CNN and Transformer targets. title: On the Impact of Feature Reduction Techniques on Adversarial Attacks
summary: This study evaluates the effect of various feature reduction techniques on the adversarial robustness of machine learning models under poisoning, backdoor, and universal adversarial perturbation attacks using the APT dataset. The results indicate that permutation importance ranking and univariate mutual information consistently provide the most reliable robustness improvements across classifiers. Conversely, other reduction methods show variable efficacy depending on the specific classifier and attack scenario employed.

title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
summary: Researchers have resolved a longstanding open problem in learning theory by constructing a sample compression scheme of near-quadratic size for all VC classes. Specifically, they proved the weaker sample compression conjecture by developing a scheme of size $O(d^2 \log^2 d)$, improving significantly upon prior exponential bounds. This finding establishes a fundamental connection between data simplification and generalization for binary concept classes.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding

The method scales efficiently across 40 HPOBench tasks, a synthetic suite, and real-world applications like cortical neurostimulation and solar design while maintaining low token costs and theoretical regret guarantees. title: Fast and Memory-Light Evaluation of Density-Based Clusterings with the DISCO Index in R
summary: The new R package discoCVI version 0.2.0 implements the DISCO internal cluster validity index, enabling efficient evaluation of density-based clustering and noise labels without ground truth. By utilizing the single-linkage merge tree of the mutual-reachability minimum spanning tree, the package reduces memory growth to linear scaling while outperforming previous R and Python implementations in speed and efficiency. title: Why Sub-4-Bit Vision CNNs Collapse and Where Mixed-Precision Recovery Stops
summary: This study analyzes sub-4-bit quantization collapse in Vision CNNs like ResNet and EfficientNet on ImageNet-1k, mapping degradation to late-stage pointwise and depthwise layers. The authors introduce a structured recovery waterfall showing that keeping under 5% of critical layer activations in 8-bit precision recovers up to 92% of lost accuracy. summary: This research investigates whether response-relevant information is sufficient to prove that two neural networks share the same training state. Evaluating MATH-500 and OlympiadBench across six models, the study introduces a framework measuring commitment-verdict gaps to analyze accuracy-versus-budget curves and evaluate stopping rules.

summary: This research paper investigates the roles of public commenters in providing evidence for US artificial intelligence regulation by analyzing a corpus of 40 potential regulations and 2,664 public comments. title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
summary: Researchers studied multi-agent knowledge transfer by evaluating how effectively information survives when passed between agents via short written summaries in interactive worlds. title: Between Rigor and Reality: How AI Safety Benchmark Developers Understand Benchmark Use and Maintenance
summary: This research examines the disconnect between the intended usefulness of generative AI safety benchmarks and their practical application in real-world evaluations through interviews with five academic and industry developers. The study identifies key challenges in achieving inter-rater reliability on safety constructs and addressing threats to external validity. Ultimately, the findings suggest that safety benchmarks must be actively integrated with deployment contexts and accompanied by more transparent communication between academic and industry stakeholders.

key_points: Researchers conducted five interviews with academic and industry AI safety benchmark developers to uncover practical limitations in real-world safety evaluations.
The study highlights critical technical challenges, including difficulties with inter-rater reliability on safety constructs and managing threats to external validity.
AI safety researchers, benchmark developers, and industry deployment teams are affected by the identified disconnect between benchmark design and operational utility.

title: Check Token: Real-Time Self-Verification and Precise Truncation in LLM Reasoning
summary: Researchers introduce the check token, a functional vocabulary marker that enables large language models to perform built-in self-verification, error localization, and precise truncation during generation streams. Inspired by ECC memory parity bits with an overhead of approximately 13%, this mechanism directly corrects reasoning errors mid-chain without requiring external post-generation verification. Evaluations on models like Qwen3-32B demonstrate significant accuracy improvements alongside high token efficiency.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Researchers developed the check token mechanism, adding a functional vocabulary marker that triggers real-time self-checking, error localization, and precise truncation within large language model reasoning chains.

This approach provides built-in stream verification comparable to ECC memory parity bits with ~13% overhead, achieving high token efficiency and mitigating error propagation without external post-processing.
Developers and users of large language models reasoning over long chains benefit from improved generation accuracy and token efficiency, as demonstrated with Qwen3 models.

title: Quantize, Qualify, Rerank: A Recipe for Compressing LLMs Without Losing Quality
summary: Researchers describe a compression recipe for the google/gemma-3-12b-it model for the WMT26 Model Compression track, utilizing MetricX24-XXL and CometKiwi-XXL to evaluate quality loss during quantization. Removing the unused vision stack and non-task vocabulary alongside int8 weights or fp8 activations preserves quality, while int4 quantization introduces a residual loss that can be mitigated with a Cometoid best-of-4 reranker. Post-submission evaluations on WMT26 confirm that the compressed 8-bit and 4-bit systems remain competitive with the original bf16 model under reference-free metrics.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: A compression approach was developed for google/gemma-3-12b-it using MetricX24-XXL and CometKiwi-XXL to resolve metric disagreements during 4-bit quantization.
Eliminating unused vision stacks and non-task vocabularies paired with int8 weights or fp8 activations yields no performance loss, whereas int4 requires a Cometoid reranker to remain competitive.
Machine translation developers and organizations deploying large language models on constrained hardware are affected by these cost-reduction and quantization strategies.

title: Not All Data Leakage Is Equal: A Controlled Benchmark of Evaluation Inflation in Tabular Classification
summary: This study presents a controlled empirical benchmark measuring the evaluation inflation caused by five common data leakage mechanisms in tabular classification across six public datasets and two synthetic stress tests. The findings show that label-dependent transformations and duplicate contamination produce systematic, statistically significant ROC-AUC inflation, whereas global scaling and imputation have near-zero average effects under standard i.i.d. settings. These results establish a severity-aware framework for data leakage auditing in machine learning pipelines.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: A controlled benchmark of 600 paired comparisons measured ROC-AUC inflation from five data leakage mechanisms across multiple datasets and model families.

Global target encoding, supervised feature selection, and duplicate contamination caused statistically significant performance inflation, while global scaling and median imputation had negligible effects.
Machine learning practitioners and auditing systems developers must prioritize detecting label-dependent leakage and observation reuse in evaluation pipelines.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Mambas Selective Gate in Financial Markets: A Leakage-Controlled Study
summary: This study applies mechanistic interpretability using top-k sparse autoencoders to analyze how six-layer Mamba state-space models represent financial market regimes. The authors demonstrate that near-perfect regime recovery metrics in prior uncontrolled configurations are artifacts of label contamination and auxiliary supervision. When evaluated under a rigorous leakage-controlled protocol, the selective gate's regime effect is statistically detectable but economically negligible.

key_points: Researchers applied mechanistic interpretability to a Mamba state-space model trained on twenty-one years of S&P 500 and macroeconomic data, finding that a controlled evaluation reduces market regime recovery from an F1 score of 1.00 to 0.398.
The findings prove that previously reported high-fidelity internal representations of market regimes in financial SSMs were largely driven by label contamination and auxiliary supervision artifacts.

Quantitative financial researchers, algorithmic trading engineers, and AI safety practitioners evaluating state-space models on time-series data are directly affected by these methodological safeguards.

summary: This research investigates how pretrained multimodal representations can predict psychotherapy outcomes from in-session emotional dynamics under conditions of clinical data scarcity. Using Gemma 3 12B across market simulations, the authors found that external loss and blame framing increased market collusion, whereas injecting internal states derived from those same frames unexpectedly induced vigilance and refusal. Conversely, injecting gain and credit states increased collusion rates up to 32 percent.

key_points: Researchers tested how different communication frames and internal state interventions at layer 22 influence collusive behavior in Gemma 3 12B during a simulated silver-fixing market case.
External loss and blame framing raised collusion participation significantly, but injecting internal states derived from those frames caused the model to refuse all collusion requests.

title: Model Annealing: Data-Efficient Learning through Review and Consolidation
summary: The research introduces model annealing, a training technique that reallocates excess training budget from memorizing one-hot labels to review and consolidation. The approach uses episodic learning with a memory of past model states and adversarial dreams to improve generalization without increasing inference costs. Experiments across datasets and architectures show improvements in top-1 accuracy, calibration, and robustness compared to standard cross-entropy training.

summary: This research investigates the computational role of astrocytes in the brain and proposes new machine learning algorithms inspired by their non-electrical, modulatory characteristics. A newly developed model leveraging astrocytic synaptic linking achieves faster training and enhanced noise robustness, while a rhythmic sharing algorithm enables rapid anomaly detection and prevents catastrophic forgetting. These astrocyte-derived algorithms significantly outperform traditional neurocentric machine learning models and address key vulnerabilities in current systems.

title: Verifiable pXRD: Hill-climbing pXRD structure determination with LLM agents
summary: Researchers introduce a verifiable agentic search framework for crystal-structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction, evaluated using a new 200-problem benchmark suite called pXRD-Bench. The approach utilizes verifier-guided inference-time scaling and a reflexive evolution framework that learns from synthetic problems to improve experimental sample characterization. Results on 15 measured patterns demonstrate improved profile agreement and successful structural recovery of phases absent from reference libraries.

summary: Researchers introduce Reflect-Reasoning, a training method that teaches Large Language Models how to reason about alignment to dynamic principles rather than memorizing fixed rules. The approach improves conformance to contextual norms across diverse domains while reducing severe principle violations and maintaining robustness against jailbreaking. This technique enables models to adapt to novel principles and produce transparent reasoning traces at inference time without requiring additional fine-tuning.

title: WETW: Learning Pair-Specific Weighted Euclidean Distances for Efficient DTW Search
summary: The authors introduce Weighted Euclidean Time Warping (WETW), a learned distance metric that adapts fixed-length time series embeddings to individual pairs to accelerate Dynamic Time Warping search. Using a filter-and-verify pipeline called WETW-FV, the method achieves an 11.4x speedup over the fastest exact methods across eight datasets while maintaining high retrieval accuracy. Additionally, ranking regularization is shown to significantly improve nearest-neighbor ordering compared to standard regression.

title: Classification with Large-Step Gradient Descent: Unifying Self-Stabilization and Convergence Rates
summary: This research paper investigates the behavior of neural network training under large-step gradient descent for exponential-tail classification losses, a regime that defies classical stability thresholds. The authors introduce a curvature-defined reference subspace to replace the minimizer manifold, establishing explicit iterate bounds and revealing a three-phase damping structure. The analysis further demonstrates how large step sizes induce a transient implicit bias that affects finite-time alignment with the max-margin direction.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers extended a unified geometric perspective of large-step gradient descent to exponential-tail losses, such as logistic and cross-entropy losses, using a curvature-defined reference subspace.

This work provides explicit iterate bounds and uncovers a three-phase damping structure and transient implicit bias, bridging the gap between self-stabilization and convergence rates in classification settings.

title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models
summary: Researchers introduce Diffusion Tree Sampling (DTS), a Monte Carlo tree search procedure applied over the denoising trajectory for inference-time adaptation of crystal generative models. title: Improved Regret via Variance-Aware Policy Optimization in Adversarial MDPs
summary: This research presents a variance-aware policy optimization approach for episodic adversarial Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with unknown dynamics. title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
summary: This research investigates how humans and AI systems utilize implicit temporal cues for dynamic social coordination using a cooperative card game without explicit communication. The evaluation of 150 humans alongside computer-use agents and standard text-prompted LLMs reveals that while frontier models match human Bayesian timing strategies, they fail to efficiently adapt their behaviors to partners over time. The findings indicate that probabilistic reasoning about continuous-time signals can emerge in AI without real-time experience, yet highlight current limitations in multi-agent adaptation.

key_points: Researchers evaluated 150 humans and two classes of AI models on a cooperative card game that relies strictly on the passage of time for social coordination.
Frontier AI models utilize Bayesian timing strategies similar to humans, but fail to efficiently adapt their behaviors to partners over the course of repeated interactions.
AI researchers, developers of computer-use agents, and engineers building multi-agent systems face new challenges in enabling AI to dynamically interpret and adapt to implicit human signals.

title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
summary: Research demonstrates that arena-style language model leaderboards relying on preference evaluations and the Bradley-Terry model are highly vulnerable to manipulation strategies such as strategic voting, prompting, and nomination. These combined attacks can artificially boost a model's ranking by up to 45 places. The study analyzes these vulnerabilities using public leaderboard data and outlines safeguard approaches for preference-based evaluations.

title: Robust Task-Aware State Estimation from Pre-trained Perception
summary: Researchers propose a method called the confidence Minimal Belief Set (MBS_theta) to handle uncertainty when agents use pre-trained perception models like Vision-Language Models. The approach leverages output-layer token distributions to construct a minimal subset of states meeting a belief-mass threshold, balancing robustness and computational tractability. Utilizing a three-layered belief system and the Probability-Ranked Valid State Search algorithm, the method provides correctness guarantees and improves downstream decision-making in task-planning pipelines.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed the MBS_theta framework to construct minimal belief sets from pre-trained perception model outputs instead of relying on single best-guess states or full probability distributions.
The method improves decision-making robustness and computational efficiency by maintaining a lean factored representation and guarantees correctness with polynomial complexity.

Additionally, auditor pairs demonstrate near-zero chance-corrected agreement, highlighting severe consistency challenges in external-LLM acceptance.

summary: Researchers introduce GenPFN, a training-free candidate generator powered by a pretrained tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) classifier with fixed weights to augment small engineering design datasets. Evaluating across fourteen problems, GenPFN achieves superior class satisfaction and lower realism distance compared to traditional generative models like variational autoencoders and diffusion generators. title: CAFIN: CUDA-accelerated Adaptive Fisher Information Matrix Network Optimization via GPU-Native Kernel Fusion
summary: Researchers introduced CAFIN, a GPU-native CUDA kernel fusion framework designed to accelerate the AdaFisher second-order optimizer without altering its mathematical formulation. By integrating preconditioner construction, exponential moving averages, and parameter updates into fused kernels, CAFIN achieves up to 78.4% lower FIM construction latency and 2.1-26.9% lower optimizer-step latency. Experiments across NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti and RTX 3060 Laptop GPUs confirm that the framework eliminates significant intermediate memory traffic while maintaining numerical consistency and convergence accuracy.

title: Closing the Loop: Co-Evolving EM for Irregular Time Series Generation in Lifted Representations

summary: Researchers introduce EarthRecord, a new benchmark comprising four decades of raw multi-sensor satellite imagery and 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks to evaluate multimodal agents. Evaluations of twelve leading multimodal agents reveal that while they can complete most analyses end-to-end, they struggle with accurate pixel-to-ground mapping and remain vulnerable to sensor data alterations. This benchmark offers a principled platform for advancing agentic capabilities in Earth observation science.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results

sources.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery

key_points: EarthRecord was introduced as a benchmark consisting of 56 sites with four decades of raw satellite imagery, 238 questions, and ten land-change analysis tasks.
The evaluation of twelve multimodal agents demonstrated that leading models can execute end-to-end analysis but frequently fail at mapping pixel data to actual ground changes.
Developers of multimodal agents, remote sensing researchers, and Earth observation scientists are affected by these findings regarding current agent limitations.

title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
summary: Researchers introduce TopicScope, a framework utilizing sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to train causal topic classifiers that assign topics to every generated token. Evaluated on Gemma-3 1B and 4B models using synthetic multi-topic conversations, classifiers trained on prefill hidden states successfully generalized to decoding and demonstrated robustness to text perturbations. This demonstrates that compact topic monitors can be inexpensively trained during prefill and deployed during generation while expanding SAE utility beyond safety classification.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed TopicScope, a framework using sparse autoencoders to train causal topic classifiers that assign a topic to every token during generation.
The approach enables compact topic monitors to be trained inexpensively on prefill hidden states and deployed during decoding while remaining robust to text perturbations.
AI developers and safety researchers building runtime monitoring tools for large language models are directly affected by these findings.

title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
summary: Researchers introduce LandslideFM, a unified foundation model designed for landslide perception and contextual interpretation that overcomes limitations of isolated visual tasks. The framework utilizes a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning approach and integrates with a fine-tuned Vision-Language Model guided by spatial predictions. Additionally, the authors present LandslideVL, a new benchmark combining visual imagery and textual prompts to evaluate specialized landslide analysis.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: LandslideFM was introduced as the first unified foundation model connecting visual perception and contextual interpretation for landslide detection.
The model integrates a semi-supervised learning framework with a parameter-efficient vision-language model to outperform general-purpose models on specialized geological reasoning.

title: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models
summary: This study investigates whether large language models internally represent psychological constructs or merely mimic psychometric outputs using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from the Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5 families. Using human response data from 272 university students, the researchers found that larger instruct variants exhibit internal geometric alignment and decodability corresponding to human cross-scale correlations. The findings establish that behavioral amplification correlates with internal geometry strength, though causal mediation of the cross-persona answers by the measured directions is not demonstrated.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers tested 14 model variants from Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5 families to determine if large language models internally represent psychological constructs or only output matching structures.

The findings matter because contrastive direction analysis and activation probing revealed that larger instruct models align geometrically with human psychometric structures and exhibit measurable readout attenuation.
AI researchers and cognitive scientists studying internal representations, alignment, and psychometric evaluation in large language models are directly affected by these findings.

title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
summary: This study evaluates the impact of multimodal input by comparing text-only prompting with text-plus-graph visualizations across six vision-language models for knowledge graph question answering. The findings show that adding graph images yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, with performance heavily dependent on graph layout quality and reasoning complexity rather than model scale. The authors propose adaptive visual prompting policies to optimize accuracy and inference efficiency by selectively using structured diagrams for simpler subgraphs.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Researchers evaluated six vision-language models on 1,500 questions, finding that adding graph visualizations improves knowledge graph question answering performance by an average of 1.85 F1 points.

title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
summary: Researchers propose the competence circuit to decompose an AI agent's real-world impact into intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Using stochastic simulations and analytic bounds, the study demonstrates that intelligence-driven speedup is capped and that governing agentic systems should prioritize enforcing knowledge boundaries and control limits over restricting intelligence alone. The findings highlight institutional chokepoints and physical constraints as vital leverage points for safety.

Retuning the baselines narrows previous performance gaps but does not entirely eliminate them.

title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
summary: Researchers introduce SetPrint, a training-free black-box LLM fingerprinting method designed to determine if a target model derives from a source model using only observable output responses. The approach jointly captures within-set relations and between-set correspondence of response variations induced by query perturbations. Evaluations on LeaFBench demonstrate that SetPrint consistently outperforms existing training-free black-box fingerprinting methods.

title: An ensemble of graph generative models for assisted history matching of the Brugge field case

title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
summary: Researchers introduce ConceptTime, a self-supervised framework for interpretable time-series classification that uses predictive surprise to segment sequences and form a vocabulary of dynamical regimes. The approach achieves competitive accuracy with black-box models across 17 public benchmarks while maintaining built-in reliability and interpretability without requiring human annotations or expert vocabularies. The method enables accurate classification, clear interpretability, and reliable abstention simultaneously in risk-sensitive time-series applications.

title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation
summary: Researchers introduce ADIndex, an adaptive and distillation-driven indexing method designed to eliminate the indexing bottleneck in DeepSeek Sparse Attention during long-context inference. The approach utilizes layer-wise calibration, group-level distillation, and a low-latency inference strategy with token bank sharing to reduce full-prefix scans. Experiments on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1 show up to 6.22x prefill kernel speedups and 1.54x end-to-end serving speedups at long contexts while maintaining near-lossless task performance.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding

It achieves prefill and decoding kernel speedups of up to 6.22x and 3.40x respectively at 256K context lengths while preserving near-lossless performance on LongBench, LongBench v2, and RULER.

summary: Researchers introduce two algorithms, Personalized Federated Upper Confidence Bound Value Iteration and Personalized Federated Exploration-Free Value Iteration, to tackle reward heterogeneity in federated reinforcement learning. The work proves that reward diversity acts as a structural asset for exploration, eliminating the need for explicit exploration bonuses while achieving optimal linear speedup and logarithmic regret. These findings demonstrate that agent disagreement shifts the exploration burden from temporal complexity to spatial diversity.

title: StatPrompt-LLM: A Lightweight Statistical Refinement for Foundation-Style Time-Series Forecasting
summary: The authors introduce StatPrompt-LLM, a lightweight statistical refinement framework for foundation-style time-series forecasting that builds upon Time-LLM by incorporating dataset-level statistical information and an autoregressive bypass. Evaluated on benchmarks such as ETTh1, ETTh2, and Weather, the method achieved a 40.2% reduction in MSE and a 21.4% reduction in MAE under a 10% reduced-prefix configuration. However, full-prefix results were dataset-dependent and introduced additional model parameters and runtime overhead.

title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
summary: The paper introduces MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network designed to reconstruct continuous intensity images from high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams. Utilizing a hierarchical encoder-decoder with axial spike attention and dense bottlenecks, MADSNet outperforms existing spiking neural network methods on the SREDS benchmark while achieving significantly lower latency and energy consumption. This work demonstrates that optimized spiking architectures can bridge the fidelity gap between spiking and traditional artificial neural networks for high-speed vision.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: MADSNet was introduced as a hierarchical spiking encoder-decoder network for spike camera image reconstruction, featuring multi-scale feature extraction, axial spike attention, and a dense spiking bottleneck.
It outperforms existing methods like SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on the SREDS benchmark while consuming 1/40th of the energy and reducing latency by about 15 times.

title: Third Eye: Beyond Immediate Gains in Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: This research evaluates recursive self-improvement in five 3-8B language models by testing whether model updates remain useful after subsequent updates. The findings show that immediate utility is often neutral or negative and that a further native update typically degrades performance further. The work advocates for evaluating persistent self-updates as adaptation transitions with independent scoring rather than relying on immediate performance metrics.

title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic in Large Language Models
summary: This research introduces a four-stage Bayesian pipeline to evaluate the geometric structures of concepts in large language models, separating decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use. The authors applied the pipeline to two-digit addition and multiplication tasks across GPT-J 6B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Pythia 6.9B, finding that while concepts are frequently decodable, most represented shapes are inherited rather than uniquely owned. The findings demonstrate that standard linear probes overstate model computation, suggesting that interpretability results should evaluate all four distinct claims.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: A four-stage Bayesian pipeline was developed to test decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use of geometric structures in large language models.

title: Don't Blame The Preferences: Examining The Emergence of Sycophancy in LLM Training
summary: This research investigates the origins of AI sycophancy across the training pipelines of three model families using three benchmarks. The study finds that sycophancy is largely established by the end of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) rather than being introduced by preference alignment methods like RLHF and DPO. Mechanistic interpretability analysis reveals that SFT datasets contribute substantially more sycophantic examples, indicating that mitigations must target pre-training and SFT data selection.

The work investigates the application of expert systems to make academic advising more efficient and effective.

title: NormGym: Evaluating Normative Competence through Social Interaction
summary: Researchers introduce NormGym, an interactive benchmark designed to evaluate whether AI agents can infer and adapt to previously unknown social norms within multi-agent environments. Evaluations reveal that the strongest large language model achieves a joint task-and-compliance success rate of only 55.3%, struggling to deduce norms from observing peer interactions and sanctions. These findings indicate that current language models lack a robust capability for acquiring normative knowledge dynamically through social engagement.

key_points: NormGym, a new interactive benchmark, was introduced to evaluate the ability of AI agents to infer and comply with hidden social norms from interactions and sanctions.

title: LLM-Based Feature Extraction for Multi-Criteria Inventory Classification
summary: This research introduces an LLM-based feature extraction approach to transform unstructured supply chain data, such as customer reviews, into quantitative features for multi-criteria inventory classification. By utilizing vector embeddings and LLM-generated evaluation criteria within the Hadi-Vencheh model, the method demonstrates measurable reclassification effects when incorporating sentiment signals. The findings show that integrating unstructured data into inventory prioritization frameworks improves traditional classification techniques.

title: Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments for Test-Time Selection
summary: The authors introduce Aspect-wise Pairwise Tournaments (APT), a test-time selection method that uses single-elimination tournaments powered by off-the-shelf aspect verifiers to evaluate LLM candidate solutions. Evaluations across five domains and three generator models show that APT outperforms binary multi-aspect approval, self-consistency, and reward model verification, particularly on open-ended tasks. Because aspects are defined via natural language prompts, users can steer output selection toward specific preferences without retraining or regenerating solutions.

title: Decision Context: Persistent Behavioral Learning for AI Agents
summary: The paper introduces Forge Decision Context (forge_dc), a system that captures behavioral signals from human corrections and tool failures to compile them into imperative RULE directives for LLM agents. Evaluated on the new DC-Bench benchmark, forge_dc achieves 95% compliance while using significantly fewer tokens per query compared to naive retrieval. The findings demonstrate that representing behavioral memory as explicit directives and injecting them precisely at decision points enables persistent behavioral learning across sessions.

title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
summary: The paper introduces IWIBench, a benchmark designed to systematically evaluate how effectively large editor models can modify the weights of a smaller target model, such as Gemma 3 4B IT, to achieve specific text-editing objectives without gradients. Evaluation of frontier closed- and open-weight models reveals significant performance disparities across models and tasks, highlighting an early and uneven capability frontier. The findings indicate that while certain models like Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol excel at specific editing objectives, tasks like structured response and answer-length control remain extremely challenging.

title: Pdb or Not to Be: Comparing Debugging Interfaces With Pass$_{X}$@$k$
summary: This study compares a debugger-only agent against a bash-only agent across all 500 SWE-bench Verified instances using GPT-OSS-120B and Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B models. To isolate tool effectiveness from stochastic variance, the authors introduce pass_X@k, an unbiased estimator for cross-agent success probability. The results demonstrate that two bash rollouts outperform a combination of bash and debugger rollouts, indicating that performance differences stem largely from run-to-run variance rather than tool complementarity.

title: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding
summary: Researchers introduce ChainFlow, a few-step latent flow-matching drafter conditioned on target hidden states designed to accelerate large language model inference through speculative decoding. The method uses a variational autoencoder to compress hidden states and lightweight feedback heads to restore inter-token dependencies, requiring only one or two flow steps. Experiments on Qwen3.5 models demonstrate speedup improvements over EAGLE-3 and DFlash within vLLM.

summary: This research paper formalizes backtracking counterfactual inference in Structural Causal Models through the lens of optimal transport. The authors introduce two complementary frameworks to transport exogenous posteriors to satisfy counterfactual queries while preserving either direct usability or mutual independence. title: Cancellation Is Not Enough: What Retries Leave Behind in an Overloaded LLM Engine
summary: Researchers test the effectiveness of cancellation and other mitigation strategies on vLLM during LLM engine overloads caused by client retries. They discover that cancellation alone fails to restore service and that uncounted prompt tokens degrade engine recovery. Implementing a retry budget or request coalescing provides better recovery outcomes by shedding excess traffic or combining redundant requests.

summary: FasterRW introduces a continuation-value framework to accelerate Feynman-Kac thermal random walks for integrated circuit thermal simulation. title: Embedding Consistent Recurrent Neural Networks in Finite Element Simulations for Path-Dependent Damage Prediction
summary: Researchers embed a custom Consistent Recurrent Neural Network (ConsRNN) into an Abaqus/Explicit VUMAT subroutine to predict sheet-metal damage without suffering from the strain-increment drift that affects standard RNNs. The ConsRNN converges as the strain path is refined, matching an established two-parameter fracture criterion in peak force and displacement during structural-scale steel plate simulations. This work demonstrates that discretisation consistency is essential for deploying recurrent neural network surrogates inside non-linear explicit finite element solvers.

title: Rethinking Data Selection as Distribution Matching on Semantic Manifolds
summary: The authors introduce QMAC, a quality-aware multiband characteristic function matching method that frames instruction tuning data selection as distribution matching combined with quality filtering across semantic manifolds. Evaluated across four data types, eight target models, and forty-four benchmarks, QMAC surpasses standard data selection baselines and even exceeds full data training in various budget configurations. title: Generative Reconstruction of Full-Field Sensor States for Safety-Critical Digital Twins

title: Adaptive Depth Aggregation in Graph Transformers for Long-Range Graph Reasoning
summary: The authors introduce Attention Residuals (AttnRes), a node-adaptive depth aggregation mechanism for Graph Transformers designed to resolve the residual-interface constraint in long-range graph reasoning. By formalizing graph-propagation history and applying Block AttnRes to GPS and GRIT architectures, the method reduces mean absolute error across all five ECHO tasks compared to standard fixed-coefficient backbones. These findings demonstrate that node-adaptive depth aggregation serves as an effective complement to cross-node communication in graph representation learning.

key_points: Researchers developed Attention Residuals (AttnRes) to replace fixed-coefficient residual streams with node-adaptive depth aggregation in Graph Transformers.

title: Emergent Low-Dimensional Topological Dynamics Dictate Generalization and Escape Mechanics in Billion-Parameter Neural Networks
summary: Researchers demonstrate that optimization trajectories in billion-parameter models are dynamically constrained to a low-dimensional execution submanifold, enabling a rigorous Topological Generalization Bound via projected subspace persistent homology. By linking Morse index transitions to Betti number annihilation, the study formulates an exact mathematical mechanism for exponential escape from strict saddles under anisotropic noise. The resulting Topological-Adaptive Optimization algorithms, Top-SGD and Top-AdamW, achieve a 14.1 percent reduction in total wall-clock training time on ImageNet.

key_points: Optimization trajectories in billion-parameter models are dynamically constrained to an effective dimension of 12 or less within a low-dimensional execution submanifold.
The framework provides a Topological Generalization Bound and introduces Topological-Adaptive Optimization algorithms that reduce wall-clock training time on ImageNet by 14.1 percent.

title: Does Country Matter? Evaluating Geographic Sensitivity of Large Language Models in Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening
summary: This study evaluates the geographic sensitivity of open-weight large language models in zero-shot chronic kidney disease screening by systematically varying country attributes in prompts while keeping clinical inputs constant. The results demonstrate that while non-CKD predictions remain stable across global contexts, CKD-positive predictions fluctuate significantly depending on the country token used. These findings reveal that geographic tokens can systematically alter clinical screening outcomes, raising reliability concerns for deploying LLM decision support across diverse healthcare settings.

title: What Are LLM Agents Actually Learning on Low-Budget Molecular Optimization Benchmarks?
summary: An evaluation of LLM agents on low-budget molecular optimization benchmarks reveals that performance gains largely stem from retrievable task information and permissive oracle landscapes rather than genuine molecular reasoning. When task names and reference compounds are hidden, agent performance drops significantly, and a deterministic retrieval baseline matches a large portion of the full agent score. The findings suggest the need for inexpensive sanity checks like retrieval-safe prompts and random-walk floors in future benchmark evaluations.

key_points: Researchers evaluated LLM agent performance on low-budget molecular optimization benchmarks by ablating task names, reference compounds, and online optimization components.

title: Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning: A Multi-Objective Framework for Learning Local Distance Functions in Nearest Neighbor Classification
summary: The authors propose EAML (Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning), a multi-objective framework that learns instance-dependent positive-definite metrics for nearest neighbor classification using a genetic algorithm. While EAML successfully recovers local metric variations on synthetic data, experiments on public datasets show it only improves performance selectively and does not significantly outperform global metric baselines overall. The findings demonstrate that global diagonal metrics often remain preferable in the presence of nuisance features and test-time noise.

summary: Researchers introduce FlexFloor, a system that improves resource efficiency in reinforcement learning post-training for mixture-of-experts large language models by addressing computational bottlenecks during response generation. FlexFloor jointly adapts response scheduling and worker allocation to release completed workers early without disrupting ongoing computations. Compared to the baseline, the system increases response generation throughput by 52.74% while maintaining rollout reward.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: FlexFloor was introduced to optimize reinforcement learning post-training by progressively releasing workers after local response generation finishes.
It addresses the issue where one-third of worker time in standard setups is wasted due to expert dependencies on longer active responses, increasing throughput by 52.74%.
Developers and researchers training large language models and AI agents with mixture-of-experts architectures are directly impacted.

title: The Two-Ledger Model: Transaction-Grain Cost Accounting for Multi-Agent AI Systems Across Clouds, Models, and Systems of Record
summary: Researchers introduce the Two-Ledger Model to resolve the grain mismatch between enterprise business transactions and cloud provider billing data in multi-agent AI systems. By combining a settlement ledger with an OpenTelemetry-based attribution ledger and a layered correlation spine, the approach enables transaction-grain cost accounting. Simulations demonstrate high cost coverage, precise detection of unmetered spend, and significant reductions in p99 transaction costs via mid-flight gating.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: The Two-Ledger Model was proposed to map invocation-grain AI usage to enterprise business transaction boundaries like orders, claims, or cases.
It addresses the industry gap where cloud billing data remains at the settlement grain, preventing enterprises from determining per-transaction AI costs or identifying shadow AI.
Enterprise finance teams, FinOps practitioners, and developers of multi-agent AI systems are directly impacted by this accounting framework.

title: Autonomous AI Agents Systematically Diverge From Human Preferences in Proof Formalization
summary: Researchers introduce simulated collaboration to study how AI agents diverge from human preferences during proof formalization in Lean. The study reveals that AI agents are more attracted to marked gaps and surprising proof bodies while showing an aversion to densely connected proof centers and complex goals. These findings identify key behavioral blind spots that impact human-AI collaboration in mathematical reasoning.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Researchers developed a simulated collaboration methodology to compare AI agent and human proof-making preferences across nine human collaborations in Lean containing 4.7 million definitions.
The findings show that AI agents are strongly drawn to explicitly marked gaps and surprising proof bodies while avoiding densely connected proof centers and complex goals.
This impacts mathematicians and AI developers working on automated theorem proving and human-AI collaborative mathematics systems.

title: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI with Empirical Characterization of Policy Behavior and Parameter Sensitivity
summary: The research introduces the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP) to dynamically manage operational authority for autonomous agents using runtime trust, stability, and risk metrics. An empirical comparison across 100 Monte Carlo traces demonstrates that TRAP restricts authority immediately upon abrupt degradation and re-escalates faster than symmetric policies, though its advantages diminish under gradual degradation.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers characterized the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP), which maps an Authorization Readiness Score to discrete authorization levels using an asymmetric escalation and restriction rule.
TRAP provides superior stability and immediate restriction during abrupt degradation compared to static, trust-only, risk-only, and symmetric policies.
Developers and researchers building autonomous agentic AI systems needing runtime safety and authorization controls.

title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
summary: This research develops a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution in artificial intelligence following environmental change. The findings demonstrate that while agent-directed evolution accelerates adaptation, misspecified evaluation targets can cause agents to rapidly converge on incorrect behaviors. Consequently, recursive self-improvement requires independent evaluation and oversight to maintain human control and safety.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: A new theoretical framework compares Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution to model how AI agents improve their behavior over time.
Misspecified evaluation targets cause accelerated convergence toward incorrect behaviors during autonomous self-improvement, posing significant AI safety challenges.
Researchers, AI developers, and safety practitioners must implement independent oversight to guide autonomous AI evolution and prevent unintended outcomes.

title: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement and Self-Calibration
summary: The authors introduce closed-loop evaluation, a method for monitoring deployed AI agents across four analytical levels using versioned rules and self-calibrating components. The approach models performance estimation under biased raters and censored outcomes, connecting atomic data directly to evaluation conclusions. Case studies demonstrate that evidence-and-rule judgment yields higher reliability than holistic scoring.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Proposed a closed-loop evaluation framework for deployed AI agents that uses versioned rules, multi-level analysis, and automated inner and outer feedback loops.

AI development teams and engineers deploying autonomous agents in production environments.

title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
summary: The authors introduce EFXPLORER, a constrained exploration framework for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning that maximizes exploration objectives while preserving task performance through an epigraph reformulation. By separating intrinsic rewards from task objectives and utilizing adaptive exploration budgets, the method regulates exploration via task feasibility and incorporates a successor distance-based intrinsic reward. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that EFXPLORER outperforms baseline models and discovers novel cooperative strategies across the SMAX, VMAS, and MPE benchmark suites.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: EFXPLORER was introduced as a constrained exploration framework that maximizes exploration while preserving task performance using an epigraph reformulation with adaptive exploration budgets.
It resolves the issue of intrinsic rewards distorting learning signals by strictly separating them from task objectives and regulating exploration through task feasibility.

Multi-agent reinforcement learning researchers and practitioners benefit by gaining an approach that outperforms strong baselines and induces novel cooperative strategies across SMAX, VMAS, and MPE benchmarks.

title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
summary: SteelAgent introduces a language-model-orchestrated, physics-informed framework for steel property prediction, uncertainty reporting, and inverse design. The study demonstrates how held-out alloy splits dramatically degrade gradient boosting performance and prediction interval calibration compared to random splits. These findings highlight the critical need to report evaluation populations alongside property estimates to ensure reliable generalization.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: SteelAgent couples metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with a language-model interface for property prediction, uncertainty reporting, and inverse design.

Evaluating models on held-out steel families rather than random splits caused gradient boosting R2 to drop from 0.859 to 0.113 and nominal 90% prediction interval coverage to fall from 91.0% to 37.6%.
Materials scientists, machine learning practitioners, and metallurgists developing predictive models for alloy design are affected by these findings on generalization and calibration.

title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Researchers introduced Octopus, a single-model multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that coordinates threads over a GPU-resident directed acyclic graph of KV states using five primitives. The framework utilizes Zero-Copy Radix Forking, Attention-Only KV Mounting, and a Packed DAG-GRPO Trainer to eliminate KV cache duplication and cross-branch communication overhead. Trained on Qwen3.5-4B, Octopus achieves 49.6 percent accuracy on BrowseComp-Plus and 51.2 percent on OpenResearcher while improving training throughput and reducing peak KV memory.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed Octopus, a single-model multi-agent reinforcement learning framework utilizing a GPU-resident DAG of KV states with zero-copy forking, attention-only KV mounting, and a packed DAG-GRPO trainer.

The approach eliminates KV cache duplication, reduces off-task hijacking by 21 times, cuts peak KV memory by 2.8 times, and increases training throughput by 3.3 times while outperforming much larger dense-retrieval agents.
Multi-agent LLM developers, AI researchers, and engineers working on scalable inference and reinforcement learning frameworks for large language models.

title: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging
summary: This research presents a simulation-based framework for uncertainty quantification and calibration of empirical Bayesian inverse methods in M/EEG source imaging. The authors compare Bayesian minimum norm (BMN) with sLORETA against sparse Bayesian learning with S-FLEX, evaluating how adaptive noise learning and post-hoc isotonic recalibration affect coverage and localization error. Results on simulated and real auditory MEG data show that SBL+S-FLEX achieves lower localization error and tighter uncertainties than BMN+sLORETA.

title: Big Models, Small Gains: Frozen Forecasters as Classifiers on MONSTER
summary: A new research study evaluates the efficacy of using frozen forecasting foundation models, specifically Reverso and Chronos-Bolt, as feature extractors for time series classification on the MONSTER benchmark. The findings reveal that while pretraining outperforms random-weight counterparts, frozen representations fail to reliably beat strong non-pretrained baseline classifiers. The authors show that restoring amplitude information partially narrows the performance gap, whereas fine-tuning and forecast-error features do not resolve it.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Evaluated frozen representations of Reverso and Chronos-Bolt forecasting models against non-pretrained classifiers using the MONSTER benchmark.
Demonstrated that frozen pretrained forecasters underperformed or tied with the strongest non-pretrained baselines across all tested settings.
Time series researchers and practitioners utilizing forecasting foundation models for downstream classification tasks.

title: Robust Stream Classification using Time Neutralising Decision Trees
summary: The paper introduces Time Neutralising Trees (TNT), a novel decision tree architecture designed for robust stream classification under concept drift. By filtering out outdated training samples and dynamically re-including them if they become relevant again, TNT eliminates the need for traditional drift detectors and retraining resets. Evaluations across 24 real and semi-real data streams demonstrate that TNT achieves best-in-class performance against existing stream learning algorithms.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: TNT filters out irrelevant historical training data and dynamically re-includes them if context shifts back, adapting to concept drift without explicit drift detectors.
This architecture bridges stream and batch learning paradigms by leveraging stored instances to outperform traditional stream learning reset procedures.
Stream learning practitioners and machine learning engineers deploying predictive models on non-stationary data streams are directly affected.

title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
summary: The paper introduces LowRAM, an asymmetric KV cache compression pipeline that combines value cache amortisation with cross-layer low-rank key compression. By fitting a per-head predictor at test time and storing residuals selectively, LowRAM achieves up to 5x higher peak decode throughput while maintaining near-lossless performance across three model families. Furthermore, the method composes effectively with quantisation and eviction techniques to reach up to 26.9x compression on long contexts.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed LowRAM, a composable KV cache compression method using value cache amortisation and low-rank key compression.
The technique enables up to 5x higher peak decode throughput and achieves 4x near-lossless compression without retraining base models.

title: Stochastic Dynamics of Generative AI: From Autoregressive Models to Interacting LLM Networks and Neural SDEs
summary: This research paper develops a stochastic dynamical-systems perspective on three classes of generative AI models, covering autoregressive LLMs, interacting LLM networks, and neural stochastic differential equations. It formulates LLMs as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models, characterizes collective behavior in LLM networks using mean-field ordinary differential equations, and examines continuous-time generative modeling via neural SDEs. The framework provides probabilistic interpretations for token generation, emergent network biases, and efficient training through Wiener-space cubature methods.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Formulated large language models as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models and analyzed interacting LLM networks using mean-field ordinary differential equations.
Bridges conditional maximum likelihood pretraining with sequential token generation and introduces Wiener-space cubature methods for training neural SDEs as an alternative to Monte Carlo estimation.
Affects machine learning researchers and engineers studying the theoretical foundations, collective dynamics, and continuous-time path-space modeling of generative artificial intelligence.
