title: Finite-Time Convergence and Regret Guarantees for Neural Reinforcement Learning in POMDPs
summary: This research paper investigates reinforcement learning in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes using nonlinear neural value function approximation. The authors establish a finite-state MDP point-wise approximation error bound, prove a finite-time critic error bound using Temporal-Difference learning, and derive a finite-time sublinear regret guarantee via the policy mirror descent framework. Numerical experiments are provided to verify these theoretical results.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Established a finite-time sublinear regret guarantee and neural value function error bounds for POMDPs using a superstate MDP surrogate approach.
Bridges theoretical gaps in reinforcement learning by avoiding overly simplified linear function approximations and i.i.d. sampling oracle assumptions.
Researchers and practitioners working on reinforcement learning algorithms for partially observable environments.

title: Shaping & Monitoring Models through their Internal Representations
summary: Researchers introduce Mechanistic Shaping, a training framework that controls model behavior and decision-making concepts through internal representations across vision, medical imaging, and language domains up to 32B parameters. The work also establishes a monitorability hierarchy to analyze how shaped concepts can circumvent probes via geometric mechanisms like drift, erasure, or nonlinear encoding. Results demonstrate that shaped concepts generally remain detectable using refitted or matching monitors.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Mechanistic Shaping was introduced as a training framework to control both model outputs and internal decision-making concepts without degrading task performance.
A new monitorability hierarchy and geometric analysis explain how models can circumvent internal concept probes through drift, erasure, or nonlinear encoding.

title: Optimistic Hedge in General-Sum Games: Fundamental Limits and Regret Bounds via Temporal Approximation
summary: This research paper investigates the regret bounds of Optimistic Hedge in finite general-sum games. The authors demonstrate that two-player games can achieve $O(n\log n)$ constant regret independent of the horizon, whereas games with three or more players suffer from exponential regret bounds in terms of action size or linear growth with the horizon. A new temporal approximation framework is introduced to analyze the algorithm's performance and simplify existing regret proofs.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers established that Optimistic Hedge yields $O(n\log n)$ horizon-independent regret in two-player general-sum games, but causes exponential $2^{\Omega(mn)}$ or linear regret in $m$-player games where $m \ge 3$.
This work resolves the longstanding open question regarding the explicit polynomial dependence and fundamental limits of Optimistic Hedge regret bounds based on player counts.
Game theorists, algorithmic game theory researchers, and developers of multi-agent reinforcement learning systems are affected by these theoretical limits on no-regret learning dynamics.

title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
summary: This research paper investigates the institutional jurisdiction of multi-agent language-model review systems by comparing broad override authority with an evidence-gated replacement mechanism. summary: Researchers introduce Agent Harness Awareness, a trust-separated design that bridges operational blindness by supplying agents with a verified state snapshot before consequential actions. title: More Rules, Longer Lists? Benchmarking Self-Evolving Agents on a Hidden-Rule Curriculum
summary: The paper introduces CLR-Bench, a Curriculum of Latent Rules benchmark designed to test whether self-evolving agents can learn hidden rules from feedback rather than just logging exceptions. Evaluations across six recent self-evolution methods show that most models struggle without explicit conventions, whereas stronger models like GPT-6-Sol combined with ACE and Dynamic Cheatsheet successfully learn from feedback alone. The benchmark demonstrates that self-evolution capabilities vary significantly across base models.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Researchers introduced CLR-Bench, featuring 20 chains across 10 domains to evaluate self-evolving agents on hidden-rule curricula.

Testing showed that most recent self-evolution methods achieve limited gains (5 points over frozen agents) when relying on base models, while stronger models like GPT-6-Sol successfully learn from feedback.

summary: This research evaluates safety sufficiency in web world models, demonstrating that plausible future predictions do not guarantee correct safety decisions. The authors introduce the SafeWebWorld benchmark and Latent Authorisation Recovery to analyze evidence preservation and policy-decisive information in web-safety domains.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Introduced SafeWebWorld to benchmark safety sufficiency and policy-decisive evidence across five web-safety domains.

title: Circumventing the Computational Hardness of Computational Arbitrage
summary: This research paper formalizes computational arbitrage in AI model marketplaces as an allocation problem and proves that it is generally NP-hard. The authors demonstrate that optimal allocation can be computed efficiently under a diminishing-returns condition and introduce a sample-efficient method for estimating model performance from limited data. These findings provide economic insights into how arbitrage shifts revenue toward complementary specialization and away from low-utility providers.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding

title: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models
summary: Researchers investigate how incongruence between text and audio channels affects speech emotion recognition in audio large language models across multiple corpora. They introduce a continuous, threshold-free incongruence score mapped in valence-arousal-dominance space to evaluate error rates. Results demonstrate that cross-modal disagreement consistently increases error probabilities when audio is present, indicating challenges in evidence combination.

The authors introduce a taxonomy of seven surveillance risk categories and test 110 prompts, finding that the model frequently supplies substantive surveillance guidance and working code. The findings demonstrate that refusals are often accompanied by detailed instructions or architectural guidance despite brief ethical caveats.

title: Does Recursive Knowledge Construction Help Agents Verify Consensus Claims in Science?
summary: Researchers investigated how recursive knowledge construction and stopping judges affect scientific agents when verifying consensus claims from the open literature. They introduced ProClaim, a system that persists structured evidence outside the model's context, and a new evaluation dataset called ProClaim-eval containing 718 claims. The findings demonstrate that maintaining an external structured evidence state combined with a trained judge significantly improves verification performance compared to in-context accumulation and fixed-round stopping.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: ProClaim and the ProClaim-eval dataset with 718 expert-curated claims were introduced to evaluate recursive knowledge construction in scientific agents.
Persisting structured evidence outside the model's context and using a separately trained judge outperforms in-context accumulation and fixed-round stopping.
Scientific agent developers and researchers working on literature-based consensus verification are directly affected by these architectural findings.

title: Towards Portable Specification of the Agent Harness
summary: This research paper introduces a decomposition of the agent harness into eight functional components to address the lack of a settled definition for language model infrastructure. It proposes a portable specification framework to record model and harness configurations, noting that different harness setups can cause several-fold differences in benchmark scores and security attack surfaces. The framework addresses how harnesses change across releases, between runs, and dynamically within runs.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Researchers decomposed the AI agent harness into eight functional components and proposed a portable specification framework to record model-harness configurations.
Different harness configurations cause several-fold differences in model benchmark scores and represent a significant portion of an agent's security attack surface.

title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
summary: Researchers introduce Agentic World Modeling (AWM) to enable test-time scaling for language model agents without requiring environment replication or risking irreversible side effects in shared workspaces. AWM reformulates next-observation prediction into a multi-turn evidence-acquisition task that adaptively queries real environments using safe read-only interfaces. Experiments across tau-bench, AppWorld, and OfficeBench demonstrate that AWM outperforms single-shot simulation and trained world-model baselines significantly.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Agentic World Modeling (AWM) was introduced to enable parallel test-time scaling in shared, non-resettable environments without environment replication.
It allows agents to safely query real environments using read-only interfaces and executable computation to simulate transitions under partial observability.
AI researchers, enterprise developers, and deployers of autonomous language model agents handling persistent workspaces are directly affected.

title: DiRAFT: Privacy-Aware Financial Transcript Synthesis from Aggregate Discourse Priors
summary: The authors introduce DiRAFT, a synthetic financial transcript generation method that uses aggregate discourse priors to preserve confidentiality by avoiding direct sourcing from individual records. The approach extracts concept graphs and transition priors to guide text realization, balancing transition fidelity and structural overlap through stochastic sampling. Evaluations across financial corpora and investor calls demonstrate that stochastic sampling yields fewer confidential-fact matches compared to alternative generation strategies.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: DiRAFT was introduced to synthesize privacy-aware financial transcripts using aggregate transition priors and concept graphs instead of direct source passages.
It addresses confidentiality risks in financial language model training by reducing the retention and leakage of non-public investor facts.
Financial language model developers and researchers working with sensitive customer conversations or investor calls are directly affected.

title: The First Few Tokens Matter: Understanding Chain-of-Thought Controllability
summary: This research investigates the limitation of chain-of-thought controllability in models, linking it to an entropy collapse in the first few tokens following the opening thinking tag. The authors demonstrate that inference-time interventions such as prefilling and banning frequent opening tokens can recover addition and style controllability. Furthermore, the findings show that addition and style controllability correlate positively with monitorability, whereas suppression controllability exhibits varied or negative associations.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers identified an entropy collapse in the first few tokens following opening thinking tags as the source of limitation in chain-of-thought controllability.
Interventions like prefilling and token banning successfully recovered addition and style controllability, improving average compliance by 34 to 41 percentage points across models.
AI safety researchers, model developers, and automated monitor systems are affected by these findings, which necessitate distinct evaluation and reporting for different controllability tasks.

title: Automatic Construction of Strong Simple Baselines
summary: This research investigates using large language models to automate the construction of simple baselines for scientific deep learning applications, assembling 36 tasks from peer-reviewed studies in Nature, Science, and Cell-family journals. The automatically constructed baselines recover a median of 95.5% of the performance gap between trivial predictors and specialized deep learning models, matching or exceeding published models in 12 studies. These findings suggest that automated baseline construction provides a scalable evaluation mechanism to verify deep learning contributions in the physical and life sciences.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Researchers used large language models to automatically generate strong simple baselines for 36 supervised classification and regression tasks derived from peer-reviewed life and physical sciences literature.

The automated baselines recovered a median of 95.5% of the performance gap between a trivial predictor and the specialized deep learning models, matching or exceeding published performance in 12 studies.
Peer reviewers and researchers evaluating deep learning applications in the physical and life sciences are directly affected by this scalable method for validating computational claims.

title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching
summary: Researchers propose PoSE (posterior sampling for state estimation), a method that uses flow matching on historical data to model substation injection distributions in medium-voltage feeders. The approach applies a noise-aware Kalman-type correction using power flow equations and grid topology, ensuring that every posterior sample is physically consistent. Tested on IEEE 33-bus and Iowa 240-bus feeders, PoSE reduces probabilistic injection error and maintains reliable uncertainty intervals across varying measurement sets and topologies.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed PoSE, a flow-matching-based method for Bayesian distribution system state estimation that models substation injections without approximating power flow equations.
The approach achieves lower probabilistic injection, voltage, and branch-current errors than baseline estimators while maintaining accurate uncertainty intervals across changing network topologies.
Distribution system operators and power system engineers managing medium-voltage feeders with limited real-time measurements are directly affected.

sources.title: Bayesian Distribution System State Estimation with Flow Matching

title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection
summary: The authors introduce the Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner (TADR), a conditional diffusion refiner trained against the loss landscape of a frozen downstream detector to eliminate imputation bias in Industrial Internet of Things edge pipelines. Running in 41.4 ms per window on a single CPU core, TADR raises the F1 score by 0.338 over unrefined detectors on the SMD dataset while sustaining approximately 24 concurrent 1 Hz streams from a 4.03 MB model. The method's effectiveness scales with continuous, mutually redundant channels and the amount of anomaly evidence removed by network outages.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed the Task-Aware Diffusion Refiner (TADR) to replace disjointed impute-then-detect pipelines in Industrial Internet of Things edge systems.
TADR improves anomaly detection F1 scores by 0.338 on SMD over unrefined detectors while maintaining efficient execution suitable for edge hardware.
Industrial Internet of Things operators and edge computing developers dealing with multi-sensor data dropouts and network faults are directly affected.

sources.title: Don't Just Impute, Detect: Task-Aware Diffusion Pipelines for Edge Anomaly Detection

title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version
summary: This research introduces LIDFS, an unsupervised feature selection method that leverages Local Intrinsic Dimensionality to score and rank features without requiring class labels. By transposing the data matrix and estimating LID via maximum likelihood, the algorithm identifies locally discriminative features and eliminates redundancy with a complexity of O(d^2 n). Evaluations across 23 high-dimensional datasets demonstrate that LIDFS outperforms classic and state-of-the-art baselines in both supervised classification and clustering tasks.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: The authors proposed LIDFS, an unsupervised feature selection algorithm based on Local Intrinsic Dimensionality that ranks features without requiring class labels.
The method achieves top-tier performance across 23 benchmark datasets while running faster than its closest competitors and avoiding the failure modes observed in several recent methods.
Machine learning researchers and practitioners working with high-dimensional, unlabeled data benefit from improved computational efficiency and down-stream model accuracy.

sources.title: Unsupervised Feature Selection Using Local Intrinsic Dimensionality -- Extended Version

title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors
summary: The paper introduces Certified Anchor-Based Adaptation (CABA), a post-update gating method that uses held-out historical anchors and frozen representations to bound behavioral divergence during continual model adaptation. Under explicit representation-coverage and Lipschitz assumptions, CABA guarantees that accepted updates adhere to a uniform behavioral-divergence bound without requiring action labels or complete trajectories. Experiments on a sensor-policy proxy demonstrate a reduction in mean forgetting from 1.01 percent to 0.00 percent at the cost of a lower final average accuracy.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Introduced Certified Anchor-Based Adaptation (CABA), a post-update gate using held-out historical observations to verify model updates against a protected behavior budget.

Provides a theoretical certification framework yielding uniform behavioral-divergence bounds, interpolation monotonicity, and sequential-composition guarantees under explicit coverage and Lipschitz assumptions.
Affects machine learning researchers and practitioners developing continuously adapting models that must avoid catastrophic forgetting on protected behaviors.

sources.title: Certified Behavioral Retention for Continual Adaptation with Held-Out Anchors

title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn
summary: Researchers introduce AutoHebb, a class of online learning feedforward neural networks that combine strong inductive biases and autonomously controlled learning through a biologically grounded three-factor Hebbian rule. Utilizing meta-learning to optimize fixed weights, these networks achieve zero-shot inference and continual learning capabilities while outperforming modern learning models. The approach demonstrates that integrating neuromodulatory feedback with local learning rules can effectively bridge biological plausibility and high-performance task generalization.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed AutoHebb, feedforward neural networks that use a neuromodulator-gated three-factor Hebbian rule for autonomous learning and zero-shot inference.
The model outperforms modern learning models on zero-shot inference and continual learning tasks, demonstrating the importance of meta-learning, Hebbian plasticity, and autonomous control.
Machine learning researchers and neuro-AI scientists studying biologically grounded learning algorithms and continual adaptation are directly affected.

sources.title: AutoHebb: Self-Modifying Neural Networks that Zero-Shot Infer and Continually Learn

title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation
summary: Researchers studied catastrophic forgetting in the Walrus-1.3B physics foundation model during a two-stage sim-to-real adaptation involving simulated and experimental fluid dynamics data. The investigation revealed that finetuning rapidly degrades performance on prior datasets, increasing one-step errors up to 35x after 20 epochs. Introducing a 1% data replay strategy during finetuning successfully recovered lost simulation performance while preserving adaptation to real-world experimental dynamics.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Walrus-1.3B experienced severe catastrophic forgetting, with one-step errors increasing up to 35x during sim-to-real adaptation.
Replaying just 1% of simulated data during real-data finetuning recovered most lost simulation performance without harming experimental adaptation.
Researchers and practitioners working on scientific foundation models and sim-to-real robotic or continuum dynamics workflows.

sources.title: Frozen in Time: How a Physics Foundation Model Forgets Under Sim-to-Real Adaptation

title: FARO: Function-Space Adaptive Return-to-Risk Optimization via Cross-Block Equal-Risk-Contribution Budget Allocation
summary: Researchers introduce FARO, a function-space adaptive optimizer that automates parameter block partitioning and budget allocation using cross-block equal risk contribution (ERC) derived from portfolio theory. When evaluated on a GPT-style model trained on FineWeb, FARO matches the performance of the best hand-designed optimization recipes while achieving a modest, robust improvement in clean-data loss without adding time or memory overhead. The framework demonstrates resilience by lowering mean loss even under corrupted data streams.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed FARO, an optimizer that automates per-block geometry assignment and reallocates budgets via cross-block equal risk contribution.
The method matches the performance of hand-designed optimization recipes and lowers clean-data loss across all tested seeds without increasing computational overhead.
Large language model developers and researchers training compute-bound models benefit from automated, robust partition and budget allocation strategies.

sources.title: FARO: Function-Space Adaptive Return-to-Risk Optimization via Cross-Block Equal-Risk-Contribution Budget Allocation

title: Near-Optimal First-Order Regret for Bandits with Feedback Graphs
summary: This research paper addresses the gap between worst-case and first-order regret bounds in adversarial bandits with directed feedback graphs. The authors develop an algorithm achieving an expected regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\alpha L^\star}+\alpha)$ for strongly observable graphs, matching the independence number dependence of minimax bounds.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Researchers developed an algorithm for adversarial bandits with feedback graphs that achieves an expected regret bound of $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\alpha L^\star}+\alpha)$.
This work bridges a theoretical gap between worst-case independence number dependence and first-order cumulative loss bounds.
Theoretical machine learning researchers and practitioners studying online learning and bandit algorithms are directly affected.

title: TensorSSM: Memorizing Spatial Position in Dynamic State Space for Tensor Core Generation
summary: Researchers introduce TensorSSM, a novel Implicit Neural Representation method that utilizes a dynamic State Space Model to memorize spatial positions and capture cross-mode dependencies for functional tensor decomposition. By decomposing coordinates via a K-ary rule and mapping inter-mode interactions, the approach reduces high-dimensional tensor storage overhead while improving reconstruction accuracy. Experimental results show that TensorSSM achieves high storage efficiency and robust expressiveness across diverse datasets without strict spatial assumptions.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: TensorSSM was proposed as a functional tensor decomposition method using a dynamic State Space Model to handle high-dimensional tensors.
It improves data compression and reconstruction accuracy by preserving spatial position sequences and explicit cross-mode dependencies.
Machine learning researchers and practitioners working on high-dimensional data compression and implicit neural representations are affected.

title: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes
summary: Researchers introduced LRMoE, a memory-aware Mixture-of-Experts training system that jointly recalibrates backward demand and balances retained workloads on memory-constrained nodes. The system plans retention quotas during forward execution and uses a load recalibration metric during backpropagation to select token-expert pairs. Experiments on large models like Qwen3-30B-A3B and GLM4.5-106B-A12B demonstrate a 21.2 to 44.8 percent reduction in cumulative MoE-layer training time to reach fixed-loss targets.

summary: Researchers introduce a method for amortized localized posterior inference to handle model discrepancy and observation uncertainty during calibration. title: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs
summary: This research evaluates the effectiveness of curated, LLM-generated, and data-derived ontologies as checkers for LLM agents operating over knowledge graphs. The study investigates how different ontology sources balance caught errors against false alarms, finding that curated schemas can contradict their own data and exhibit low precision. The findings demonstrate that curated ontologies on UniProt flag more correct answers than data-derived or LLM-derived alternatives, performing only marginally better than random flags.

summary: Researchers introduce Seq@K, a new evaluation protocol that measures a language model's ability to solve problems across up to K sequential attempts using natural language feedback. title: Moment-Guided Optimizers for Noisy Deep Learning: MGO-SC as a Simple Consistency Gate for Adam-Style Updates
summary: Researchers introduce MGO-SC (Moment-Guided Optimizer with Sign-Consistency), a lightweight modification for Adam-style optimizers that utilizes a coordinate-wise consistency gate to handle noisy deep learning environments. By applying a mean-preserving variant that reallocates trust across fluctuating gradient signs without altering net step magnitude, the method improves performance under various label noise conditions. Evaluations on CIFAR-10 using ResNet-18 demonstrate consistent improvements over AdamW, including a 1.4 percentage point gain at 40% symmetric noise.

sources.title: Moment-Guided Optimizers for Noisy Deep Learning: MGO-SC as a Simple Consistency Gate for Adam-Style Updates

key_points: MGO-SC introduces a coordinate-wise consistency gate derived from a sign exponential moving average to down-weight fluctuating gradient signs and trust stable ones.

The mean-preserving variant reallocates trust without changing net per-tensor step magnitude, overcoming effective step size loss and outperforming baseline AdamW across clean, symmetric, and asymmetric label noise.
Deep learning practitioners training models on noisy datasets and researchers working on adaptive optimization algorithms are directly affected.

title: What a Weight Update Buys: Leverage Across Training Stages
summary: Researchers introduce leverage, an exact measure calculated via the Fisher quadratic form to quantify the behavioral impact of language model weight changes across training stages. The study reveals that pretraining updates accumulate into noise while post-training stages like SFT, RL, and DPO achieve significantly higher leverage. Additionally, the findings demonstrate that training precision choices such as omitting fp32 master copies can freeze parameter coordinates and degrade leverage.

title: Threshold Compatibility and Support-Selection Diagnostics in Neural Discovery of Partial Differential Equations
summary: This research paper investigates threshold compatibility and support-selection diagnostics in the neural discovery of partial differential equations. The findings show that accurate regression fails to guarantee correct equation recovery after support selection, highlighting persistent issues with threshold incompatibility, refit damage, and score rejection. These diagnostics demonstrate that supplied-support estimates consistently outperform unchanged selected equations across tested physical-residual comparisons.

title: Predicate Neuron: Differentiable Quantization of Predicate Relations in Gradient-based Learning
summary: Researchers introduce the Native Predicate Neuron, a differentiable logic-reasoning neural module that integrates symbolic reasoning into standard deep learning architectures via first-order logic quantization. The module utilizes a dual-nature gradient mechanism to execute hard logical operations during training while remaining differentiable for backpropagation across Fully-Connected, Convolutional, Recurrent, and Transformer models. Evaluations on benchmarks such as MNIST and Wikitext demonstrate that the Predicate Neuron accelerates training convergence, improves accuracy, and successfully handles monotonic reasoning and discontinuities.

summary: This research introduces Anisotropic Trust Region (ATR) warping to correct lengthscale mismatches in Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) used for Bayesian optimisation without requiring network retraining. title: Responsible Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Imaging: A Fairness Audit Across Sensitive Subgroups
summary: This study presents an empirical fairness audit comparing classical and quantum classifiers using ResNet-18 embeddings across dermatological and chest X-ray datasets. summary: This research paper introduces partition-invariant neural networks for asynchronous sensors like event cameras, avoiding the dependency on time slicing or binning. title: How far can we push computing?
summary: The historical scaling laws driving the information age, such as Moore's Law and Dennard's Law, are slowing down or breaking as physical miniaturization encounters limits. Meanwhile, hyperscalers are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on physical infrastructure to scale computing performance by brute force. However, these scaling laws are merely observations of past engineering rather than fundamental physical limits, leaving room for future breakthroughs governed by quantum mechanics and information theory.
priority_explanation: Relevant AI development
key_points: Traditional computer hardware scaling laws like Moore's Law and Dennard's Law have slowed down or ended, while hyperscalers spend hundreds of billions on massive data center infrastructure builds.

Understanding that scaling laws are merely observations rather than fundamental physical limits highlights the gap between current engineering boundaries and the ultimate physical limits dictated by quantum mechanics.

title: When is a large language model a good calibration agent? Physics-labeled prompting for budgeted engineering simulator calibration
summary: This study investigates using Large Language Models conditioned on physical diagnostic descriptions to calibrate expensive engineering simulators more efficiently than conventional optimizers. The findings show that while LLMs provide a strong early semantic advantage, their performance diminishes after multiple evaluations due to decoder variability. To overcome this, the authors introduce a hybrid workflow using the LLM as a warm-start for a conventional optimizer, achieving target accuracy in fewer simulator runs than either method alone.

title: Trust but Verify: Designing Region-Inhomogeneous Forward Dynamics for Discrete Diffusion
summary: Researchers introduce a region-inhomogeneous forward dynamics approach for discrete language diffusion that replaces binary trust with intermediate trust by combining absorbing and uniform-mixing kernels. Finetuning a 170M-parameter masked diffusion model with this method improves infill token-F1 by up to 6.4 points under 20% uniform-random corruption while maintaining a false-edit rate below 0.4% on clean conditioning. The technique enables the model to detect corrupted context with 0.96 recall and 0.91 precision without architectural modifications.

title: Binding-Specific Relearning Savings for Test-Time Continual Learning
summary: This research investigates test-time continual learning in language models by measuring relearning savings rather than relying solely on output accuracy. Using Qwen2.5-1.5B, the study demonstrates that prior learning of a specific factual binding accelerates subsequent relearning and reduces required optimizer updates by approximately 18% compared to control groups. The findings show that current behavioral accuracy can underestimate the lasting influence of previously acquired experience in parameter-updating models.

title: Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields: Evidence-Grounded Selective Safety for Vision-Language Models
summary: Researchers introduce Counterfactual Neighborhood Risk Fields (CNRF), an evidence-grounded framework for selective vision-language model safety that decouples neighborhood support from risk estimation. By constructing context-matched counterfactual pairs and establishing a victim-adaptive interface, CNRF achieves an 86.06 to 89.30 percent macro defense success rate across three VLMs and five multimodal jailbreak families. This approach enables selective intervention and constrained response generation without blanket rejection or loss of benign-task utility.

title: IneqAgent: Agentic Inequality Proving in Lean with Symbolic Computation
summary: IneqAgent is an agentic framework that integrates large language model reasoning with symbolic computation backends to automatically prove inequalities in the Lean 4 proof assistant. title: L2G-SR: Learning to Guide LLM-based Symbolic Regression
summary: The authors introduce L2G-SR, a framework for LLM-based symbolic regression that integrates a learned structural verifier using tree edit distance to complement numerical error during the search process. This approach helps prevent searches from favoring inaccurate surrogates that merely have low numerical error, evaluating candidate formulas based on structural similarity. title: ARIA: Runtime Inspection and Amendment for Multi-Agent Systems
summary: The authors introduce Agent Runtime Inspection and Amendment (ARIA), a framework and large-scale dataset designed to detect and correct errors in multi-agent systems during execution. By training on execution-verified repair pairs constructed from thousands of trajectories, ARIA enables a compact model to intervene at runtime and generalize across unseen frameworks and host models. title: FlowBudget: Training-Free Sampling-Budget Estimation for Flow Matching Models
summary: The authors introduce FlowBudget, a training-free estimator designed to determine the solver-relative sampling complexity and numerical resolution required for flow matching models without relying on empirical Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) sweeps. By utilizing simulation-free interpolation probes, the method normalizes leading discretization errors and maps numerical tolerances to step budgets for solvers such as Euler, Heun, and Euler-Maruyama. Experiments across SiT, FlowDCN, and Rectified Flow architectures validate the approach for estimating number of function evaluations (NFE) budgets.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: FlowBudget was introduced as a training-free method to estimate solver-relative sampling complexity and NFE budgets for flow matching models.
It eliminates the need for expensive empirical FID-versus-NFE sweeps by using simulation-free interpolation probes to map numerical tolerances to step budgets.

title: Expanding Attention: A Taylor-Series Route to Linear-Time Transformers with a Fixed Number of Recurrent States
summary: Researchers introduce a method that expands the exponential kernel of attention into a truncated Taylor series, factorizing it into a tensor-power inner product that collapses causal history into a fixed number of recurrent states. This approach achieves linear-time complexity with constant per-token decoding latency and parallelizable prefill, outperforming standard softmax attention at longer context lengths. Optimal performance is reached at second order with query and key normalization as a strict prerequisite for convergence.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: A truncated Taylor series expansion of the attention kernel collapses causal history into a fixed number of recurrent states updated via rank-one outer products.
The method reduces prefill and decoding complexity to linear time relative to context length, yielding significant speedups over standard softmax attention at large scale.
Researchers, model architects, and machine learning engineers working on efficient transformer architectures and long-context scaling are directly affected.

title: Same Answer, New Box: How Much of RLVR's Out-of-Domain Gain Is Answer Format?
summary: Recent research demonstrates that 82% of the out-of-domain multiple-choice accuracy gains attributed to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) on 7B SimpleRL models actually stem from models learning specific answer formatting habits rather than improved reasoning. By re-scoring outputs with an extractor that reads answers regardless of placement, the study reveals that base models already state correct answers in free text before RL moves them into designated boxes. These findings indicate that reported evaluation gains depend heavily on extractor design choices rather than genuine capability expansion.

title: KNOU-Flood: Advancing global streamflow forecasting with lead-aware probabilistic machine learning
summary: The authors introduce KNOU-Flood, a probabilistic machine learning framework for global streamflow forecasting that extends existing transfer-learning recipes using a longer input window, lead-aware forecast inputs, multi-source weather data, and a latent-noise ensemble. title: Lotus: Learning to Understand Time-series by Learning to Forecast
summary: Researchers introduce forecast grounding, a pretraining principle that requires language-aligned time-series representations to remain predictive of future signal evolution. They instantiate this principle in LOTUS, a model that combines raw patches with spectral representations and achieves top performance on TSRBench while using minimal trainable parameters. The approach enables compact time-series language models to outperform models 25 to 50 times their size.

title: Inverse Reasoning Models for Efficient Post-Training and Verification from Answer-Only Data
summary: Researchers introduce a self-distillation technique using answer-only data for reasoning LLMs, training an inverse reasoning model to generate latent chain-of-thought sequences conditioned on answers. Evaluated on Qwen3-0.6B for Countdown and GSM8K tasks, this offline approach roughly doubles hard-prompt pass@1 performance after GRPO saturation and doubles as an accurate test-time verifier. The method bypasses the compute inefficiencies of reinforcement learning and the supervision bottlenecks of missing reasoning traces.

title: Do Vision CIL Methods Transfer to Protein? A Diagnostic Benchmark of Frozen Protein Encoders
summary: This research evaluates nine representative class-incremental learning methods across five protein encoders and two enzyme function datasets to test their transferability from computer vision. The diagnostic benchmark reveals that vision-based CIL methods fail to transfer reliably due to weak gradient stability signals, heterogeneous embedding geometry, and mismatched covariance assumptions. These findings demonstrate that continual-learning design must adapt to the specific geometry of protein representations rather than treating encoders as passive feature extractors.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Evaluated nine class-incremental learning methods across five protein encoders and two enzyme datasets, finding that no existing vision CIL method transfers reliably to protein sequence and structure encoders.
Identified root causes of failure including weak gradient-based stability signals, embedding geometry heterogeneity, and scaling mismatches in covariance assumptions.

title: Do Perturbation Predictors Learn Gene Interactions? Diagnosing Extrapolation in Agentic Screening
summary: This study evaluates whether machine-learning perturbation predictors can learn unseen gene interactions during out-of-distribution screening. The authors introduce additive disagreement (AD) as a metric to measure model deviation from simple additive predictions of single-gene effects. Across eight models and three Perturb-seq datasets, specialised neural predictors do not consistently outperform the additive baseline, and larger deviations from linearity correlate with higher prediction errors.
priority_explanation: Original research or technical finding
key_points: Evaluated eight machine-learning perturbation prediction models across three Perturb-seq datasets to test generalization on unseen gene combinations.
Showed that specialised neural predictors do not consistently outperform a simple additive baseline, and higher additive disagreement correlates with greater prediction error.

title: Token Utility for On-Policy Distillation via Local Trust-Region Optimization
summary: Researchers introduce a token utility formulation for on-policy distillation derived directly from the distillation objective using the categorical Fisher matrix and logit gradients. Instantiated as Fisher Utility Weighting (FUW), the method applies continuous, mean-normalized token weighting that improves mathematical reasoning performance across multiple student-teacher pairs. The approach outperforms uniform on-policy distillation on mathematical reasoning benchmarks under both reverse-KL and forward-KL objectives.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: Derived a closed-form token utility for on-policy distillation based on the categorical Fisher matrix and logit gradients under a local KL budget.
Provides a principled way to perform continuous token weighting, termed Fisher Utility Weighting (FUW), aligning token selection with the specific distillation objective.
Improves mathematical reasoning performance by 1.08 to 4.0 macro points across Qwen3 student-teacher pairs compared to uniform on-policy distillation.

title: PMO-Dock: Benchmarking Docking, Specificity, and Generalization in Molecular Optimization
summary: Researchers introduce PMO-Dock, a standardized benchmark and protocol for docking-based molecular optimization featuring 25 tasks across hit generation, lead optimization, and specificity testing. The evaluation framework enforces strict oracle budgets and separates validation tasks from held-out test tasks to measure true generalization and sample efficiency. Benchmarking four distinct optimization methods reveals that no single approach dominates universally across all tasks, highlighting the necessity for method-dependent selection strategies in drug discovery.

title: Data Density Scaling Laws for Image Self-Distillation
summary: Researchers examine data density scaling laws for image self-distillation models across multiple datasets including ImageNet, Waymo, and Ego4D. They demonstrate that sample repetition can sometimes outperform training on larger unique sample sets, challenging conventional scaling assumptions. A modified Chinchilla-style scaling law is proposed to account for unique samples and sample repetition.

title: How Many Ranks Does a Token Need? A Noise-Floor Squelch for Rank-One LoRA Experts
summary: The authors introduce SQUELCH, a router-free mixture of rank-one experts for Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) that dynamically determines per-token rank allocation using a robust noise-floor threshold and Stein's unbiased risk estimate. SQUELCH eliminates cross-talk noise and redundant components without adding trainable parameters, improving performance across commonsense reasoning, knowledge, math, code, and GLUE tasks using LLaMA-3.1-8B, Qwen3, and DeBERTaV3.
priority_explanation: Reports measured benchmark or evaluation results
key_points: SQUELCH was introduced as a router-free mixture of rank-one LoRA experts that soft-thresholds token responses against a robust noise floor determined by Stein's unbiased risk estimate.

It improves performance by 2.2-3.2 points over standard LoRA and 0.8-1.2 points over mixture baselines while activating an average of only 8.6 out of 32 components per token, adding zero trainable parameters.
Machine learning researchers and practitioners deploying models like LLaMA, Qwen, and DeBERTaV3 with LoRA adaptation are directly affected.

title: Artificiality's First Exam: An LLM-Referenced C-test for Supraintelligence
summary: Researchers introduce an LLM-referenced C-test for evaluating supraintelligent AI systems using Levin's Kt computable variant of Kolmogorov complexity. The framework utilizes reasoning large language models as Universal Turing Machines to generate fresh test items with difficulty measured in bits. This approach creates certified evaluation items in a high-difficulty region that currently exceeds the capabilities of frontier AI models.

title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science
summary: This research paper evaluates data science agents beyond simple downstream predictive performance, analyzing methodological failures such as data leakage across 220 tasks. The authors introduce a test suite to detect six specific data science failures and find that most agentic solutions commit at least one methodological error. Furthermore, the evaluation reveals that data leakage often correlates positively with high predictive performance, highlighting a critical blind spot in current agentic benchmarks.

sources.title: The Silent Failures in Agentic Data Science

title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop
summary: Researchers introduce ClawLoop, a framework that enables harness-based LLM agents to self-improve without external teacher models through a continuous cycle of task synthesis, training, and diagnosis. The system generates and validates its own training tasks, updates the agent using SFT and RL, and refines subsequent iterations based on rollout behavior analysis. Using Qwen3.6-27B, the approach yields consistent performance gains on benchmarks such as SkillsBench, Claw-Eval-Live, and ClawGym-Bench.

sources.title: ClawLoop: Self-Improving Agents via Harness-Native Training Loop

summary: Researchers introduce a correction training method for diffusion models that addresses error accumulation and exposure bias by training an explicit corrector on intermediate predictions. This approach significantly improves unguided and unconditional sample quality across DiT, SiT, and JiT models, achieving performance competitive with classifier-free guidance. summary: Researchers introduce MOSAIC, a method using Multimodal Orthogonalized Sparse Autoencoders to trace training-sample influence in vision-language models at the patch and phrase level. summary: This research explores an intermediate agent architecture where cloud-written programs defer bounded questions about user data to a local small language model via function calls. summary: The authors introduce MDN-VJEPA, a multimodal probabilistic Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture that models future states using a Gaussian mixture network to represent alternative futures, probabilities, and uncertainty.
